newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures soft in line with dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures soft in line with dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished lower in dull trade, as market participants focused on the precious metals market where palladium futures tumbled by their limit-lows at the opening, traders said on Monday.
"Volume's so thin (in the aluminium market). I don't want to burn my hands," one trader at a major trading house said.
"It's not worth paying attention (to aluminium) when precious metals are moving so wildly."
TOCOM benchmark April 1998 shed 0.9 yen to finish at 195.1 yen per kg, reflecting the dollar's retreat against the yen.
The metal's slight fall in London on Friday also undermined prices, traders said.
Estimated trade volume was 1,250 lots, a record low after 1,671 lots on Tuesday last week.
Other contracts were also weaker excluding nearby October which added 0.4 yen. Turnover in the October contract was just one lot.
In London on Friday, three-month aluminium failed to make any upside progress finishing $3.00 lower at $1,619 per tonne.
